# Incident Report — MTA-2026-01-31

**Capture window:** 2026-01-28 03:04:03 – 03:14:27 (UTC+4), 51,181 frames / 26.4 MB, single LAN segment 10.1.21.0/24.

## 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (NetBIOS/workgroup name observed as WIN11OFFICE) |
| AD domain | WIN11OFFICE.COM (DC at 10.1.21.2, WIN-LU4L24X3UB7) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString, realm WIN11OFFICE.COM, frames 214–50727) |

Confirmed by cross-referencing DHCP Request (frames 1/3, hostname DESKTOP-ES9F3ML, requested IP 10.1.21.58, client MAC 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2), NBNS name registration (DESKTOP-ES9F3ML<00>/<20>), and gratuitous ARP (00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 → 10.1.21.58).

## 2. Malware family

**Attribution is behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No file hash could be recovered — the dropped payload was downloaded entirely over TLS 1.3 and no key log or exported object is present in the evidence, so it cannot be hashed or matched to a signature. Internet lookups were not used per the task constraints.

What the traffic shows: a fake-software-download delivery chain (landing page → intermediate download page → payload host, all sitting behind Cloudflare) followed by execution of a payload that performs a browser/system fingerprinting check-in to a dedicated PPI-style "gate" server before further redirection. This is consistent with a **commodity Windows loader/infostealer distributed via a Pay-Per-Install malvertising chain** (the fingerprint-and-report gate pattern — enumerate each installed browser, POST `id`/`token`/`agent` to `/api/set_agent`, then `act=log` — matches the delivery-gate behavior documented for Lumma Stealer-class loader campaigns), but the specific family name cannot be certified from packet capture alone.

## 3. Timeline

| Time (rel.) | Event |
|---|---|
| +45.3s | DNS query + TLS session to **hiyter.com** (104.21.22.231) — landing page, 8 KB |
| +45.8s | DNS query + TLS session to **media.megafilehub4.lat** (104.21.48.156) — intermediate download page, 217 KB |
| +48.3s | DNS query + TLS session to **arch.filemegahab4.sbs** (104.21.46.67:443) — **16 MB payload downloaded**, TLS 1.3, over 22.4s |
| +90.3s | TLS session to **whooptm.cyou** (62.72.32.156:443) — post-execution check-in/gate |
| +92.3s → +123.0s | Repeated HTTP/HTTPS beaconing to **whitepepper.su** (153.92.1.49) — fingerprint collection and exfil (see §4) |
| +122.8s | TLS session to **holiday-forever.cc** (80.97.160.24:443) |
| +126.5s | TLS session to **communicationfirewall-security.cc** (104.21.9.36:443 / 172.67.141.109:443) |

## 4. Indicators of compromise (all observed directly in the pcap)

**C2 / gate endpoints (IP:port):**
- 153.92.1.49:80 and 153.92.1.49:443 — **whitepepper.su**, primary fingerprinting/reporting gate (nginx/1.29.1)
- 62.72.32.156:443 — whooptm.cyou
- 104.21.46.67:443 (also resolves 172.67.136.13) — arch.filemegahab4.sbs, payload host
- 104.21.48.156:443 (also resolves 172.67.154.67) — media.megafilehub4.lat, download-page host
- 104.21.22.231:443 (also resolves 172.67.207.145) — hiyter.com, landing page
- 80.97.160.24:443 — holiday-forever.cc
- 104.21.9.36:443 / 172.67.141.109:443 — communicationfirewall-security.cc

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- hiyter.com
- media.megafilehub4.lat
- arch.filemegahab4.sbs
- whooptm.cyou
- whitepepper.su
- holiday-forever.cc
- communicationfirewall-security.cc

**Malicious URLs (observed in cleartext HTTP, tcp.stream 99 and follow-ons):**
- `GET http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `POST http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `GET http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `POST http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

Bot/session identifiers embedded in the URLs: `id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`, `token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`. Each POST enumerates one browser installed on the host (Chrome, then Edge), consistent with browser-targeted credential/session-theft reconnaissance.

**File name referenced by the C2 (delivery attempt, not confirmed successfully transferred):**
- `172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip` — returned in plaintext by whitepepper.su in response to the `act=log` POST ("cant open archive 172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip"), frames 24616 and 25300. This is a per-visitor packaging name (`<public-IP>-<32-hex-char-hash>.zip`); the server-side archive build failed both times, so no confirmed successful transfer of this file was observed.

**SHA256 hashes:** none recoverable. The only large binary transfer in the capture (16 MB from arch.filemegahab4.sbs, 104.21.46.67:443, TCP stream starting frame 2776, +48.365s, 22.4s duration) is fully TLS 1.3 encrypted; no TLS key log is present in the evidence directory, so its contents cannot be extracted or hashed from this capture.

## 5. Scope note

All internal Kerberos/LDAP/SMB2/DCE-RPC traffic to 10.1.21.2 (drsuapi, samr, lsarpc) is routine domain-controller/AD activity and shows no signs of lateral movement or credential abuse originating from 10.1.21.58 beyond normal domain logon traffic. No other host on the /24 shows contact with the malicious infrastructure listed above.
